title: [CLO Beginner's Guide] Materials_Button and Buttonhole
description: CLO Beginner's Guide, Material-Related Series Courses. Understand CLO fabrics and master the methods of representing garment materials, including buttons, textures, interfacing, edgings, zippers, topstitching, sewing wrinkles, and hardware accessories. This course will take you in-depth to learn how to proficiently use CLO materials.

Open the project file "material," draw a curve, paste the picture, paste it again, then add a curve and a buttonhole for it.  
Select the curve tool in the 3D toolbar.  
In the 2D window, click on the curve position, left-click to add a curve.  
The 3D window can be operated in the same way.  
Left-click and hold the curve tool, then click on the buttonhole tool to add a buttonhole on the other side of the collar.  
In the 3D toolbar, click on the curve tool.  
In the 2D or 3D window, click on the curve, then click on the buttonhole.  
When a small lock icon appears on the curve in the 3D window, and the curve arrow in the 2D window points to the buttonhole, it means they are synchronized.  
To cancel the synchronization, use the curve tool to left-click on either the curve or the buttonhole.  
The curve and the buttonhole can be unsynchronized.  
Thank you for your attention.  
Next, we will change the size and properties of the button and buttonhole.  
In the object window, select the button.  
In the property editor, you can enter the name and product number of the button.  
Click the triangle on the right side of the sample.  
You can change it to another button shape.  
The four-hole button can also be adjusted to the stitch type.  
From cross to parallel or square.  
Here, the sample is selected as 2, Shank, Button, 04.  
Under the specifications, the width, thickness, and weight of the button and buttonhole can be changed.  
Under the width, the button and buttonhole can be adjusted together.  
In this way, the button and buttonhole specifications will also change correspondingly.  
Note that this function must be used when the button and buttonhole are combined.  
Use the button and buttonhole combination.  
Adjust the width, thickness, and weight of the button and buttonhole.  
Next, change the type and color of the button and buttonhole material.  
Then, change the type, material type, and color of the button and buttonhole.  
Switch to the tool to select and move the button and buttonhole.  
In the 2D or 3D window, select the button and buttonhole.  
You can move their position.  
In the property editor, you can adjust the angle of the button and the stitch length.  
Next is the collision setting.  
The default collision between the button and buttonhole is enabled.  
This means there is a collision relationship between the button and the fabric when the model is simulated.  
The button and buttonhole can be fully simulated on the fabric surface.  
In specific cases, if the button and fabric should not collide, you can disable the collision.  
Measure the position in 2D.  
The default is off.  
Turn it on to show the endpoint of the button and buttonhole in the 2D window.  
According to the distance from the outer edge of the fabric, select the middle buttonhole.  
In the property editor, you can adjust the angle of the buttonhole.  
Adjust the buttonhole to a horizontal position.  
Based on the distance along this axis, you can adjust the vertical distance between the buttonhole and the fabric on the plane.  
You can also adjust the stitch position.  
You can see that the adjustment position of the button and stitch line can be to the left, right, or center.  
You can also display the 2D measurement position.  
Next, add the button and buttonhole to the garment.  
Add them one by one.  
There is a faster way to add them.  
Select the button and buttonhole tool.  
At the first button and buttonhole position on the garment, click.  
Add the button and buttonhole.  
Switch to the option to move the button and buttonhole tool.  
Select this button and buttonhole.  
Select copy.  
Then click the button again.  
Select paste.  
There will be a button and buttonhole attached to the mouse cursor.  
Move it with the mouse.  
At the second button and buttonhole position on the fabric, click again.  
A window will pop up.  
Enter the number of buttons.  
After confirming the number, the buttons will be added.  
Select the button and buttonhole.  
Right-click the button.  
Select to copy the buttonhole to the symmetrical fabric.  
The buttonhole is added.  
Next, I will explain the meaning of other options in the menu after right-clicking the button and buttonhole.  
Use the option to move the button and buttonhole tool.  
Right-click the button and buttonhole in the 3D or 2D window.  
Then click the button and buttonhole tool and select the menu.  
Select "Re-burn 3D position."  
The button can be reset to the simulation position.  
You can paste to one button or multiple buttons.  
You can also select and copy a single button.  
Paste multiple buttons at once.  
The operation method is the same as the above installation.  
You can also delete selected buttons.  
Duplicate to symmetrical edit panel.  
To the symmetrical panel.  
Select the button to convert into a buttonhole,  
and the button to convert into a buttonhole.  
You can also reverse activation and freeze the buttonhole.  
Select the layer to be sewn.  
You can set the sewing layer  
under the multi-layer panel.  
The flip function is used to switch the button  
to the front or back of the fabric.  
Click on the button on the buttonhole  
to select the buttonhole.  
The selected menu options are similar to the buttonhole.  
Switch to the buttonhole tool.  
Select the buttonhole,  
and click on the button after the arrow points to the corresponding buttonhole.  
Combine the buttonhole and buttonhole.  
After the simulation is stable,  
turn off the simulation.  
Select the buttonhole or buttonhole in the object window.  
The attribute editor  
will save it in the object window.  
The current buttonhole and buttonhole  
will be saved as .btn files.  
When needed,  
drag the buttonhole from the object window  
to the object window.  
Or select the default buttonhole  
in the object window.  
Click on the button in the attribute editor  
to open the buttonhole.

chunks.content: # CLO Beginner's Guide: Materials - Button and Buttonhole This guide covers the creation, synchronization, customization, positioning, and management of buttons and buttonholes in CLO software, focusing on technical operations, property adjustments, collision settings, and efficient workflow techniques. --- ## Creating and Synchronizing Curves with Buttonholes This section explains how to create curves and add buttonholes in both the 2D and 3D windows, including synchronization between curve and buttonhole elements. - Open the project file named **"material"**. - Use the **Curve Tool** from the 3D toolbar. - In the 2D window, click to place curves by left-clicking; the same applies in the 3D window. - To add a buttonhole, hold the curve tool, then select the **Buttonhole Tool**. - Place the buttonhole on the other side of the collar or desired position. - Synchronization occurs when a small lock icon appears on the curve in the 3D window, and the curve arrow in the 2D window points to the buttonhole. - To unsynchronize the curve and buttonhole, left-click either with the curve tool on the curve or the buttonhole. - Synchronization links the curve and buttonhole, ensuring they move and adjust together. --- ## Adjusting Button and Buttonhole Properties This section details how to modify button and buttonhole specifications, including size, shape, stitch type, and materials. - Select the button in the **Object Window**. - In the **Property Editor**, enter the button's name and product number. - Click the triangle beside the sample to change button shapes. - For four-hole buttons, adjust stitch types among cross, parallel, or square configurations. - Example: Sample "2, Shank, Button, 04" used. - Adjust **Width**, **Thickness**, and **Weight** for both button and buttonhole. - When buttons and buttonholes are combined, width adjustments affect both simultaneously. - Change the **Type** and **Color** of button and buttonhole materials. - Modify the button and buttonhole materials independently or together. - Use the **Select and Move Tool** to reposition buttons and buttonholes in 2D or 3D windows. - Adjust the button's angle and stitch length in the property editor. --- ## Collision Settings Between Button, Buttonhole, and Fabric This section explains the collision simulation settings in CLO for realistic interaction between buttons, buttonholes, and fabric surfaces. - By default, collision between buttons, buttonholes, and fabric is **enabled**. - This setting ensures buttons and buttonholes simulate properly on the fabric surface. - To disable collision (for specific cases where interaction is not desired), toggle collision off. - Use 2D measurement options to show or hide button and buttonhole endpoints. - Adjust buttonhole position relative to fabric edges and axis distances. - Modify stitch positions to left, right, or center alignment. --- ## Positioning and Adding Multiple Buttons and Buttonholes This section covers efficient methods to add, copy, paste, and position buttons and buttonholes on garments. - Add buttons and buttonholes one by one or use faster methods: - Select the button and buttonhole tool. - Click the first button position on the garment to add button and buttonhole.

chunks.content: - Adjust buttonhole position relative to fabric edges and axis distances. - Modify stitch positions to left, right, or center alignment. --- ## Positioning and Adding Multiple Buttons and Buttonholes This section covers efficient methods to add, copy, paste, and position buttons and buttonholes on garments. - Add buttons and buttonholes one by one or use faster methods: - Select the button and buttonhole tool. - Click the first button position on the garment to add button and buttonhole. - Switch to the move tool, select the added button and buttonhole, and copy. - Paste the copied button and buttonhole; the cursor attaches to the new element. - Move and click to place at the second position. - A window prompts for the number of buttons to add; confirm to add multiple buttons. - To mirror buttons and buttonholes on symmetrical fabric: - Select button and buttonhole. - Right-click the button and choose "Copy to symmetrical fabric." - Use right-click menu options on buttons and buttonholes for advanced operations like: - Re-burn 3D position (reset simulation position). - Copy and paste multiple buttons. - Delete selected buttons. - Duplicate to symmetrical edit panel. - Convert buttons to buttonholes and vice versa. - Reverse activation and freeze buttonholes. - Set the sewing layer under the multi-layer panel. - Use the flip function to switch buttons between front and back fabric sides. --- ## Managing Buttonhole and Buttonhole Files and Simulation States This section explains saving, loading, and managing buttonhole files and their simulation states. - After simulation stabilizes, turn off simulation. - Select buttonhole or buttonhole in the object window. - The **Attribute Editor** allows saving buttonhole properties. - Buttonhole and buttonhole configurations are saved as **.btn** files. - To reuse buttonholes: - Drag from the object window into the garment. - Or select default buttonholes from the object window. - Opening buttonholes for editing is done through the attribute editor by clicking the associated button. --- # Summary This guide provides detailed instructions on creating and managing buttons and buttonholes within CLO software, including synchronization with curves, property customization, collision handling, efficient placement, and file management for garment design projects.
